subsystems.name: High-energy particle source
subsystems.role: creates the extreme conditions needed to free quarks from protons and neutrons.

subsystems.name: Quark-gluon plasma containment
subsystems.role: holds the plasma of free quarks and gluons long enough to work with it.

subsystems.name: Femto-scale manipulators
subsystems.role: hypothetical tools that could exert forces on individual quarks or gluons at 10^-15 m.

subsystems.name: Assembly and stabilisation
subsystems.role: combines quarks into new hadrons or nuclei, or builds ordered structures.

subsystems.name: Diagnostics and control
subsystems.role: measures and steers processes at the femtometer scale.

buildSteps.title: Create a controlled quark-gluon plasma
buildSteps.detail: Today, heavy-ion collisions at facilities such as the Large Hadron Collider and the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider produce quark-gluon plasma for about 10^-23 seconds. A femtotechnology would need to make and hold such a plasma far longer.

buildSteps.title: Solve colour confinement
buildSteps.detail: Quarks are never found alone in nature; the strong force confines them inside protons and neutrons. No known method can isolate a quark, so a new understanding of the strong force would be required.

buildSteps.title: Build femtometer manipulators
buildSteps.detail: Devices would need to grip and move objects roughly a million times smaller than a nanometre. This implies position control and field generation far beyond any existing instrument.

buildSteps.title: Assemble new hadrons or nuclei
buildSteps.detail: Once individual quarks could be held, they would be guided together to form chosen combinations, effectively synthesising matter at the nuclear level.

buildSteps.title: Scale to bulk material
buildSteps.detail: A single event is not a technology. Making macroscopic amounts of material would require repeating the process at enormous rates while managing heat and radiation.

buildSteps.title: Integrate power and cooling
buildSteps.detail: The energy densities involved are like those inside particle accelerators. A practical system would need compact, high-power sources and efficient cooling.

buildSteps.title: Ensure safety and containment
buildSteps.detail: Any release of quark-gluon plasma or high-energy radiation must be contained. This would demand shielding and fail-safe designs comparable to or beyond nuclear reactors.

prerequisites.why: they are the only tools that can reach the energies needed to break hadrons into quarks.
we can create this state of matter briefly in colliders, but not control or sustain it.
quantum chromodynamics explains why quarks are confined, but no known way exists to break that confinement at low energy.
no instrument today can position matter with the required accuracy or exert forces on individual quarks.
the energy per particle needed is orders of magnitude beyond routine laboratory capabilities.

pathway.milestone: routine study of quark-gluon plasma in heavy-ion collisions
pathway.unlocks: a basic understanding of how quarks behave when freed from hadrons.

pathway.milestone: theoretical breakthrough on manipulating the strong force
pathway.unlocks: a possible route to controlling quarks, if colour confinement can be overcome.
proof that femtotechnology is physically possible at all.
materials and reactions impossible today — but only if the physics permits it, which is highly uncertain.
